note: Synthetic offline acceptance fixture. No hardware measurement or real paper claim.

source.title: Synthetic draft-budget evidence
source.body: In our synthetic example, a smaller draft budget avoids wasted verification work at high load. The author reports a 25 percent latency reduction only in the example workload; this is not a measured result from the target deployment.

claim.claim_text: The example author attributes lower high-load latency to less verification work.
claim.quote: a smaller draft budget avoids wasted verification work at high load

reported_metric.conditions: synthetic example only; not target B200/H200 evidence
reported_metric.quote: 25 percent latency reduction only in the example workload

card.statement: A load-dependent draft budget may reduce exposed verification work on the configured target.
card.mechanism: Reduce wasted verification when accepted progress falls at high load.
card.proposed_change: Prototype a bounded budget selector using retained acceptance traces.
card.falsification_test: CPU replay: reject the accounting model if committed-token accounting disagrees with trace totals.
counterevidence: Acceptance and queueing may offset any saved verification time.

brief.objective: long-output ITL with separate tail guards
